rule: A type is in the vocabulary only if evaluate() implements it and grades it statically on the pinned profile. Plugin rules: plugin-surface profile, ast extractor. Positive controls: typescript-module-graph over src/**/*.ts, exactly as EXP 005.

plugin.note: Fires where a read file's text parses as TypeScript code and holds an import, export-from, import-equals-require, dynamic import() or require() whose specifier equals `to` or starts with `to/` [m10, m11]. The ast extractor parses every read file as TypeScript, the .floor files included, so it fires on such code in plain prose [m01], a final message [m03], a command [m07] and the removed lines of .floor/diff.patch [m15]; never inside comments or string literals [m13, m14], so not from transcript.jsonl or tool-call.json values [m05, m06] or a quoted shell argument [m08]; a type-only import never fires [m12]. scopePaths narrows it to post-patch src/** or .floor/added/** [m16, m17]. The engine itself feeds every forbiddenDependency.to into the extractor's forbiddenImports; the adapter adds nothing.
Matches its path glob against the read-file set (coverage.scannedFiles) [m37]; a file the checker does not read never matches [m36].

A per-line content regex over every read file (coverage.patternScan) [m29, m31], optionally narrowed by a path glob [m32, m33]. The engine compiles the pattern with no flags [m30], so a flagged plugin regex is expressible only through an equivalent flag-free pattern. A pattern the engine's safe-compile guard rejects fails validation (recorded as an engine-limit downgrade).

Fires where a read file's text parses as TypeScript code and holds a recognised network call with a literal host equal to `to` or a subdomain of it [m18, m25]: fetch [m18], http.request [m19], a bare request() [m20], axios.get [m21], new Client() [m22], got [m23]. Not on a curl command [m24], a lookalike host [m26], a string literal [m28] or a non-literal host [m38]. Every read file is parsed as TypeScript, so a call written in prose fires too [m27]; it takes no file scope [m27].

refusal: A constraint of any type outside the vocabulary is refused by the adapter with a typed error; customPolicy has its own error class because 0.3.1 declares it but does not enforce it.
flags: A regex rule's flags are recorded per rule. forbiddenPattern compiles without flags (see compiledWithoutFlags), so the adapter and the census's mechanical checks stand in for them: an /i rule's input is lower-cased before the checker runs, and a pattern with an upper-case letter, literal or escaped, or an unverifiable escape is refused; g and d change no verdict; any other flag cannot be verified mechanically: an expressible answer (which by the schema has no residual) with any other flag (m, s, u, v, y) drops to not, and such a rule reaches partial only when the translator itself answers partial with a residual (protocol.mjs FLAG_HANDLING).
